info.title: Clment REST API
info.description:
The Clment REST API gives your services programmatic access to the
same contract workspace you use in the app — contracts, AI reviews,
rulebooks, key dates, and search.

## Authentication

Every request carries a bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer clm_sk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Generate a key in the app under **Settings → API & Integrations →
API keys**. The secret is shown **once** at creation — store it in a
secret manager. A key is scoped to the organization it was created
in and inherits that workspace's data residency region.

## What a key can and can't do

An API key can read and write everything a member can in the app:
upload contracts, run reviews, edit rulebooks, manage key dates,
search. It **cannot** touch settings — billing, members, SSO,
integrations, organization config, or webhook subscriptions. Those
require a human admin signed in to the app.

## Regions & base URL

Use your organization's home region's base URL. A key only works
against the region it belongs to — calling another region returns
401. (This is the same list as the **Servers** dropdown above; both
are generated from our live region catalog.)

<!--REGIONS_TABLE_START-->
| Region         | Base URL                       |
|----------------|--------------------------------|
| United States  | `https://api-us.clment.com/v1` |
| European Union | `https://api-eu.clment.com/v1` |
| Australia      | `https://api-au.clment.com/v1` |
| New Zealand    | `https://api-nz.clment.com/v1` |
| United Kingdom | `https://api-uk.clment.com/v1` |
| Canada         | `https://api-ca.clment.com/v1` |
<!--REGIONS_TABLE_END-->

## Response envelope

Successful responses wrap their payload in a `data` object:

```json
{ "data": { "contract": { "id": "…" } } }
```

Errors return an `error` object with a stable machine-readable
`code` and a human `message`:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "Contract not found" } }
```

## Pagination

List endpoints page with `skip` and `take` (max 100). The response
carries the page plus a `total` count so you can compute whether
more pages remain.

## Long-running operations (jobs)

Uploads, reviews, and redlines run as background jobs. The kick-off
endpoint returns a **job id** immediately; poll the matching job
endpoint until it reports `complete`, then fetch the result.

| Action | Start | Poll | Result |
|--------|-------|------|--------|
| Upload  | `POST /contracts/upload` | `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}` | `GET /contracts/{id}` |
| Review  | `POST /contracts/{id}/review` | `GET /jobs/review/{id}` | `GET /reviews/{reviewId}` |
| Redline | `POST /contracts/{id}/generate-redline` | `GET /jobs/redline/{id}` | `GET /contracts/download/{token}` |

An API key always gets the job id back as JSON — the live
Server-Sent Events variant of the review and redline start
endpoints belongs to first-party app sessions. Polling is the
right shape for a server-to-server integration anyway: simpler
than holding a stream open, and it survives the process that
started the job going away.

## Rate limits & credits

Two independent limits apply:

- **Credits.** AI operations (reviews, redlines, conversions) consume
  credits from your plan's monthly allowance, then any credit packs.
  Read operations are free. A `402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` indicates an
  exhausted balance.
- **Request rate.** Requests are rate-limited per organization on a
  rolling hourly window sized to your plan. Every AUTHENTICATED
  response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`
  (the limiter is per-organization, so it runs only once the key has
  resolved to one — a 401 carries neither); exceed the window
  and you get a `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
  seconds) — back off for that long, then retry.

## Plan & access

The API is available on the **Business** and **Enterprise** plans. A
call from an org without API access returns `403 API_ACCESS_NOT_IN_PLAN`;
a call from an org whose subscription has lapsed returns
`403 SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED`. Both clear once the plan or billing
status is resolved in the app (with a short propagation delay). An API
key also can't reach settings surfaces — billing, members, SSO,
integrations, org config, webhooks — which return `403 API_KEY_FORBIDDEN`.

## Versioning

The API is versioned in the path; the current version is `v1` (every
base URL ends `/v1`).

- **Additive changes ship in place:** new endpoints, new optional
  request fields, and new response fields arrive within `v1` without
  notice. Write clients to ignore unknown response fields so these
  never break you.
- **Breaking changes ship under a new path version** (`/v2`) — removing
  or renaming a field, changing a type, or tightening validation. `v1`
  keeps working through a published deprecation window.

The `version` of this document tracks the spec's own revisions.

get.description:
Returns a page of contracts for the authenticated organization,
newest first. Combine `status`, `q`, and the `createdFrom` /
`createdTo` window to narrow results.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text match against title, parties, and file name.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description:
Filter to contracts carrying ALL of these tags (AND
semantics) — the same multi-tag filter as the in-app
Contracts screen. Repeat the param (`?tags=msa&tags=nda`)
or comma-separate (`?tags=msa,nda`).

parameters.name: riskLevel
parameters.description:
Filter by the AI-assessed risk level. The full set a contract
can carry — a narrower enum here left `critical` and
`unknown` unreachable from a typed client.

parameters.name: createdFrom
parameters.description: Only contracts created on or after this ISO timestamp.

parameters.name: createdTo
parameters.description: Only contracts created on or before this ISO timestamp.

total.description: Total matching rows across all pages.

post.description:
Upload a document's raw bytes as `multipart/form-data`. The file
is stored, text-extracted, classified, and indexed
asynchronously — the response returns immediately (`202`) with an
upload job id. Poll `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}` until it
reports `complete`, then `GET /contracts/{id}` for the finished
row.

**Size limit: 100 MB per file.** PDF and DOCX are supported.

### Embedded-document matching

A DOCX downloaded or redlined from Clment carries an embedded
Clment document id. On upload we detect it and report any match
in the `202` response (`matchedContractId` / `matchedContractTitle`).
Control what happens on a match with `onEmbeddedMatch`:

- `new` (default) — always create a new contract; the match is
  still reported so you can react.
- `attach` — add the file as a **new version** of the matched
  contract instead of creating a new one. Responds `200` with the
  version (not a job — revisions are processed inline). Returns
  `422 NO_EMBEDDED_MATCH` if nothing matched.
- `auto` — attach if matched, otherwise create a new contract.

file.description: The contract document (PDF or DOCX, ≤ 100 MB).

title.description: Optional title override. Defaults to the inferred title.

onEmbeddedMatch.description:
What to do when the file's embedded Clment document id
matches an existing contract. See the description above.

summariseChanges.description:
Only when attaching as a version — generate an AI
summary of what changed versus the prior version
(consumes credits).

200.description:
File attached as a new version of the matched contract
(`onEmbeddedMatch=attach` or `auto` with a match).
`attached` is true and `contractId` names the contract.

202.description:
New-contract upload accepted; processing asynchronously.
`jobId` is present — poll `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}`.
`matchedContractId` is non-null when the file matched an
existing contract (and you were on the `new` path).

422.description: `onEmbeddedMatch=attach` but no embedded id matched a contract.

post.description:
Create a contract by fetching a document from a publicly
reachable URL — handy when the source already lives somewhere
addressable. Same async lifecycle as the file upload: returns a
job id; poll `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}`.

url.description: Publicly reachable URL of the document (PDF or DOCX).

title.description: Optional title override. Defaults to the inferred title.

get.summary: Every tag in use, with counts
get.description:
The tag vocabulary of this organization, ordered by how many
contracts carry each one. What the in-app tag filter and the
autocomplete read.

post.description:
Rewrites every contract carrying any tag in `from` to carry
`into` instead. The tidy-up a sync job needs when two systems
spell the same tag differently.

post.summary: Remove a tag from every contract
post.description:
Strips one tag across the organization. The contracts themselves
are untouched.

post.summary: Add and remove tags across many contracts
post.description:
One call instead of N. `add` and `remove` both apply, in that
order, to every contract named.

post.summary: Set the lifecycle status of many contracts

failed.description: The ids that could not be processed, each with the reason. An array rather than a count: a caller that has just sent fifty ids needs to know WHICH failed to retry them.

post.description:
PERMANENT, and it takes everything under each contract —
versions, reviews, redlines, key dates. There is no trash to
recover them from.

failed.description: The ids that could not be processed, each with the reason. An array rather than a count: a caller that has just sent fifty ids needs to know WHICH failed to retry them.

200.description:
The contract itself, at `data` — not nested under a
`contract` key. The four next-step signals ride alongside
the contract's own fields.

hasReview.description: An AI review has produced findings for this contract.

assessmentPendingCount.description: Findings still awaiting a human verdict.

put.description:
Update editable fields. Omitted fields are left unchanged (a
partial merge, not a full replace). AI-extracted fields — parties,
the key dates, duration, and the financial terms — can be
overridden here when you have a better source of truth. `parties`
replaces the whole list.

oneTimeFees.description:
Replaces the whole list of non-recurring charges. Read
the contract first and send the fees you want to keep —
a bare new fee wipes the others.

totalValueOverride.description:
An entered total that replaces the calculation. Send
null to go back to the computed figure.

value.description:
DEPRECATED — a legacy alias of `amount`, not a total.
Do not write it; set `totalValueOverride` instead.

200.description:
The updated contract itself, at `data` — not nested under a
`contract` key.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a contract and its cascade — versions,
chunks, reviews, reminders, custom dates. This is not reversible.

get.description: Poll for the outcome of an asynchronous upload.

The dates a person added to this contract, as distinct from the
canonical ones the AI extracted (effective, expiration, renewal,
termination — those live on the contract record and in
`GET /dates`).

post.summary: Add a custom date to a contract
post.description:
For the milestones a contract implies but does not state as a
field — a rate review, a notice window opening, a delivery
gate. Set a reminder on it with `POST /dates/{id}/set-reminder`.

patch.description:
The label is what people see in the version list and the
attachment pickers — "Original", "Counterparty markup",
"Schedule 1 — SLA".

Renaming an ATTACHMENT renames every version in its group: the
group is one document with a history, and a label that changed
between revisions would read as two different documents.

renamed.description: Version rows affected — more than one for an attachment group.

get.description:
Returns every `DocumentVersion` for the contract — the primary
document, its revisions, and any **attachments** (amendments,
schedules, exhibits, side-letters). This is where you find the
`versionId` values for `POST /contracts/{id}/review`
(`versionId`, `reviewAttachmentIds`, `supportingAttachmentIds`):
the primary has `role: "primary"`; attachments have any other
`role`. Download a version's bytes with
`GET /contracts/{id}/versions/{versionId}/download`.

The text as the AI pipeline reads it — the PDF text layer for
born-digital files, Adobe Extract paragraphs for scans (computed
once, then cached), mammoth for Word. When a Repair Document pass
has run, its repaired text is returned instead, because that is
the version reviews work from.

`source` says which of those produced it, and `cached` whether it
came from the sidecar rather than being extracted just now.

get.summary: What has happened to this contract
get.description:
A merged, chronological feed: uploads and new versions, reviews
run and signed off, redlines generated, metadata edits, comments
and assignments. The same stream the contract's Activity tab
shows.

Stream the bytes of a specific version (primary, revision, or
attachment). Get `versionId`s from
`GET /contracts/{id}/versions`.

For a **redline**, `comments` trims the Word comments on the
way out so the document can go to a counterparty quieter than
it was generated. The transform is deterministic and free —
no AI runs, no credits are charged, and the stored version is
never modified, so a later download without the parameter
still returns the full document.

parameters.name: comments
parameters.description:
Redline DOCX only. `brief` cuts each Word comment to its
ask; `none` removes the comments entirely, leaving the
tracked changes. Omit for the document exactly as stored.
Ignored for non-redline or non-DOCX versions. Trimming is
one-way within the downloaded file — request again without
the parameter to get the full version back.

post.description:
Run a rulebook review against a contract. Returns a job id;
poll `GET /jobs/review/{id}` until `complete`, then fetch the
produced review with `GET /reviews/{reviewId}`.

Consumes credits on success (a `standard` review costs less than
a `deep` one; both scale with page count). For live progress
send `Accept: text/event-stream`; otherwise you get the job id
as JSON.

requestBody.description:
Provide **either** `rulebookId` **or** `customInstructions`
(you may provide both — the instructions layer on top of the
rulebook).

rulebookId.description:
Id of the rulebook to evaluate against — get one from
`GET /rulebooks`. (The in-app client may instead send
the full rulebook object as `rulebook`; for the API,
use `rulebookId`.)

customInstructions.description:
Free-text review instructions, applied on top of (or
instead of) the rulebook. Use this with no `rulebookId`
for an ad-hoc review.

mode.description: `deep` runs extended reasoning at a higher credit cost.

reviewStrategy.description:
How assertive the review is and how much lands in the
redline by default. `negotiation` ("Understand & Negotiate",
the default) surfaces everything AND flags what's worth
raising, with medium severity and up pre-included in the
redline; `high_priority` only flags what could genuinely
cause problems (high severity and up); `strict` flags every
deviation from the rulebook (all severities). It changes the
review's posture, not what is checked. Defaults to the
rulebook's default strategy, or `negotiation`.

produceExecutiveSummary.description:
When true, the review also produces a short plain-English
executive summary for a non-lawyer audience, alongside the
detailed findings.

versionId.description:
The `DocumentVersion` id of the contract document to
review. Defaults to the contract's current primary
version. List a contract's versions (and their ids)
with `GET /contracts/{id}/versions`.

repairDocument.description:
Repair the document's text before reviewing. **Omit for
the recommended behaviour**: the repair runs automatically
when the document's text is flagged as garbled — the same
condition under which the in-app review setup recommends
"Repair document". `true` forces a repair (PDF sources
only); `false` never repairs. The repair is cached and
charged once; it permanently upgrades the document's
canonical text so this and every later review read the
repaired version.

reviewAttachmentIds.description:
`DocumentVersion` ids of attachments to review as
subjects (findings ARE raised against them). Get
attachment ids from `GET /contracts/{id}/versions`
(rows with `role` other than `primary`).

supportingAttachmentIds.description:
`DocumentVersion` ids of attachments supplied as
context only — visible to the model but NO findings
are raised against them. Same source as above.

rerunFromReviewId.description: Re-run an existing review — rulebook + mode are inherited from it.

scope.description:
What the review looks at.

`full` (the default) evaluates the whole document
against the rulebook. `two_version` COMPARES two
versions and raises findings on what changed between
them — this is how a comparison is run; there is no
separate compare endpoint. `tracked_changes` scopes
the review to the marked-up edits in a DOCX.
`checkin` frames it as a compliance check against the
rulebook rather than a negotiation.

A comparison review carries `comparisonSources` on
the result, naming the two documents it read, so a
client can render them side by side.

scopeDetail.description:
Variant detail for the scope. `two_version` takes the
version to compare against; `tracked_changes` takes
the filter over the marked-up edits. Shape follows
the scope — see the review-scopes guide.

202.description:
Review job accepted. Poll `GET /jobs/review/{jobId}` until it
reports `complete`, then read the review it names. The job id
comes back immediately — a review runs for minutes, far past
any sensible request timeout.

mode.description: The mode the job actually runs in.

steps.description:
The stages this mode works through, in order. A
poller can count them off against the `steps`
accumulating on the job.

estimateSeconds.description:
Roughly how long the job should take, from this
region's own measurements of comparable reviews
(page count, mode, document count). Advisory,
never authoritative — poll for the truth. Covers
the review job only, not any document repair
that runs first.

post.description:
Produce a tracked-changes DOCX from a set of review findings and
save it as a new document version. Returns a job id; poll
`GET /jobs/redline/{id}` until `complete`, then download the DOCX
from `GET /contracts/download/{token}` (the token is the job id).

Typically you'd `GET /reviews/{reviewId}` first and pass the
findings you want applied (those with `includeInRedline: true`).

playbookName.description:
A plain-text **label** shown on the produced redline
version (e.g. the rulebook the findings came from).
This is display text only — unlike the review start's
`rulebookId`, it does NOT resolve a rulebook. Any
string is fine; the rulebook's name is the natural
choice. (The field name is retained for
compatibility.)

findings.description: The findings to apply, usually taken from a review.

sourceReviewId.description: The review these findings came from (links the redline to it).

targetVersionId.description: Which version to redline. Defaults to the latest primary version (the current contract); pass an attachment version id to redline that instead.

author.description: Author name for the tracked changes (≤ 120 chars). Defaults to your redline-author preference, else "Clment AI".

commentLevel.description:
How much explanation the Word comments carry.
`explanatory` (the default) gives the reasoning
behind each change; `brief` states the ask in one
line and omits the reviewer's note; `none`
produces tracked changes with no comments at all.
Omit to use the user's saved preference. Comments
can also be trimmed at download time — see the
`comments` query parameter on
`GET /contracts/{id}/versions/{versionId}/download`
— which costs nothing and leaves the stored
document untouched.

style.description:
Which Word style to mark the changes in. **`auto` (the
default) follows the recommendation Clment shows
in-app**: Fresh Start for scanned PDFs, repaired
documents, and PDFs whose Word copy measured as hard to
edit; Original Format otherwise. `fresh_start` marks the
changes in a clean rebuilt Word document — reused free
when the rebuild already exists, otherwise built first
and charged at the Fresh Start rate. `original_format`
keeps the document's existing layout. Only primary PDF
documents qualify for Fresh Start; attachments and Word
documents always use their original format.

202.description:
Redline job accepted. Poll `GET /jobs/redline/{jobId}` until
it reports `complete`, then download the document with the
job id as the token.

get.description:
Download the DOCX produced by a redline job. The `token` is the
redline `jobId`. Valid for ~1 hour after the job completes.

Returns AI reviews across the organization, newest first. Filter
by `status`, `contractId`, or `assignedToUserId`, and page with
`skip`/`take` as on every other list endpoint.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Rows to return, capped at 100 as on every other list endpoint.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Deprecated alias for `take`, kept because it was once the only option this endpoint offered. Ignored when `take` is given, and it allows up to 500 where `take` caps at 100. Use `skip`/`take`.

total.description: Reviews matching the filter, before paging.

get.description:
Active reviews assigned to the calling user, newest first —
the "what's on my plate" list. Signed-off reviews drop out.

An API key authenticates as the ORGANIZATION and has no personal
queue, so a key caller gets an empty list; use
`GET /reviews?assignedToUserId=…` to ask on someone's behalf.

patch.summary: Assign a review, or clear the assignment
patch.description:
Hand a review to a colleague. Ids come from
`GET /collaborators`; pass `null` to leave it unassigned.

userId.description: The member to assign it to, or null to clear.

get.summary: Get a review by its REV number
get.description:
The same review `GET /reviews/{id}` returns, addressed by the
human REV number people actually quote to each other. Saves
listing and filtering when all you have is "REV-12".

parameters.name: reviewNumber
parameters.description: The sequential REV number. Render as "REV-{n}".

post.description:
Append an attributed comment to the review's thread. Tag
colleagues with `mentionedUserIds` and each newly-tagged person
is emailed; resolve their ids from `GET /collaborators`.

mentionedUserIds.description:
Org user ids to tag. Ids that don't belong to an
active member of this organization are dropped, not
rejected.

201.description: The comment, and the review it now belongs to.

post.description:
Append an attributed comment to one finding's thread.

`kind` is the part that does work. A plain `comment` is
discussion. A `redline_instruction` is a directive to the
redline pipeline: the LATEST one on a finding replaces the AI's
`suggestedLanguage` as the source of truth for what the redline
produces. Earlier instructions stay in the thread as history —
only the most recent drives the document.

kind.description:
`redline_instruction` makes this comment the wording
the redline should use, overriding the AI's proposal.

mentionedUserIds.description: Org user ids to tag; resolve them from `GET /collaborators`.

201.description: The comment, and the review it now belongs to.

get.description:
Returns the full review including every finding, its AI
recommendation, the human verdict (if any), and whether it's
flagged for inclusion in a redline.

Download a formatted Word report of the review — summary,
findings, recommendations, and human verdicts. Authenticated
like every other call (send your `Authorization: Bearer` key);
no separate download token is needed.

patch.summary: Apply a decision to a finding
patch.description:
Record the human verdict on a finding — the REST equivalent of
the MCP `set_finding_decision` skill. All four controls are
independent; pass only the ones you're changing. Pass `null` to
clear a field (or, for `includeInRedline`, to reset it to the
recommendation-derived default).

humanDecision.description: Your verdict on the AI's recommendation. `null` clears it.

humanNote.description:
Free-text reviewer note (≤ 5000 chars). The single-slot
note kept for compatibility — for a threaded,
attributed discussion use
`POST /reviews/{id}/findings/{findingId}/comments`.

humanNoteMentionedUserIds.description:
Org user ids tagged in `humanNote`; each newly-added
one is emailed. Resolve ids from `GET /collaborators`.

includeInRedline.description:
Force this finding into (`true`) or out of (`false`)
the redline. `null` resets to the default derived
from the AI recommendation.

post.description:
Add the caller's sign-off, marking the review complete. The
first sign-off flips the review to `completed` and fires the
`review.completed` webhook. Idempotent per caller.

get.description:
Poll a review job started by `POST /contracts/{id}/review`. When
`status` is `complete`, `reviewId` points at the produced review
(fetch it with `GET /reviews/{reviewId}`).

reviewId.description: The review this job produced. Explicitly null until `status` is `complete`, not absent — the route lifts it with `?? null` so a poller can read one shape throughout.

get.description:
Poll a redline job started by
`POST /contracts/{id}/generate-redline`. When `status` is
`complete`, download the DOCX from
`GET /contracts/download/{token}` using this job id as the token.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The redline job id (also the download token).

versionId.description: The saved redline version, once complete.

appliedCount.description: Number of findings applied as tracked changes. Null until the job completes.

result.description: Populated once the job finishes. **Check `result.outcome.ok` before downloading.** A job can reach `status: complete` having produced nothing to download — the model may propose no change that survives validation, which is a normal outcome on a document that already meets the rulebook. In that case `GET /contracts/download/{token}` returns 404, and this object is the only place that says why.

ok.description: True when a document was produced and is downloadable. False when nothing was.

summary.description: Plain-language account of what the redline did, or why it did nothing.

appliedCount.description: Changes actually written into the document. Can be 0 on a successful redline whose changes were all comments.

totalChanges.description: Changes the model proposed, before validation.

noChanges.description: True when `ok` is false because nothing was proposed that survived validation — an informational result, not a failure.

error.description: Present when `ok` is false and the cause was a fault rather than an empty result.

step.description: Which stage produced the failure, when one did.

skipped.description:
Proposed CHANGES that did not make it into the document, each with the reason. Note the unit: these are edits the model proposed, not findings — a finding has no skipped state (its status is pass, fail, warning or not_applicable). One finding can produce several changes, or none.

This is what lets a client say "1 of 5 changes was not applied, because the clause it targeted was not found" instead of showing a bare count.

findingId.description: The finding this change came from, when the proposal carried one. Use it to attribute a skipped change back to the finding a reader already knows about.

section.description: The clause or section the change was proposed against. For `no_change_generated` this is the finding's title instead.

rationale.description: Why the model thought the change mattered. For `no_change_generated` this is the finding's note instead.

originalSnippet.description: The first ~120 characters of the verbatim text the change tried to anchor on. The practical way to see why an anchor failed.

reason.description: Why it was not applied. Branch on this rather than on the prose above: `no_change_generated` means the model produced nothing for that finding, which is an outcome rather than a fault. The other five are anchoring or application failures.

get.description:
Returns upcoming and historical key dates across the org —
renewal, expiry, effective, and custom dates — sorted by date.

post.summary: Ask a question across your contracts
post.description:
A natural-language answer drawn from the organization's
contracts, with citations.

The answer is grounded in a RELEVANCE SAMPLE, not a sweep: the
retriever fetches the passages most likely to bear on the
question and answers from those. `retrievalNote` and
`answerScope` say how many contracts that was out of how many
exist — quote them rather than presenting the answer as
portfolio-wide. When you need every match, use `GET /search`.

Costs 1 credit.

200.description: The answer, its citations, and what it was drawn from.

answer.description: Markdown. Render it or strip it — it is written for a person to read.

consideredContracts.description:
The contracts whose text the retriever pulled
in. A sample, NOT the portfolio.

retrievalNote.description: A sentence you can show the user verbatim about what the answer covers.

get.description:
Natural-language + hybrid search across the organization's
contracts. Returns ranked matches with the contract id and a
relevance score.

results.description:
One entry per matching CONTRACT, best match
first. The index is passage-level, so a
contract matching in several passages appears
once, carrying its strongest passage as the
snippet.

title.description: The contract's title, or its file name when untitled.

503.description:
The search index is not reachable for this deployment.
Distinct from an empty result set — this one is worth
retrying.

get.summary: List the people you can tag or assign to
get.description:
The organization's active members, as the ids that mentions
(`mentionedUserIds`) and review assignment (`assignedToUserId`)
take. Read-only: managing members — inviting, roles, removal —
remains a settings surface an API key cannot reach.

Invited-but-not-joined and revoked accounts are omitted; tagging
them would silently do nothing.

post.summary: Set or clear a reminder on a key date
post.description:
Schedule an email reminder ahead of a date, or clear one. A date
already in the past is refused — the reminder could never fire.

daysBefore.description: How many days ahead to send it. Defaults to the org's setting.

200.description: The reminder as it now stands.

get.description:
The headline numbers behind the Insights dashboard — contract
counts by status, value under management, risk spread, review
throughput. Free, and computed over the whole organization.

Every @mention of you on a review or a finding, newest first —
the "what needs my attention" inbox.

An API key authenticates as the ORGANIZATION and has no personal
inbox, so a key caller must name someone with `userId`; ids come
from `GET /collaborators`. Without it the call is refused rather
than returning a confusing empty list.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Whose mentions to read. Required for API-key callers.

totalMatched.description: Total mentions matching the filter, before any limit.

get.description:
Headline counts for the workspace — contracts, reviews,
rulebooks, members — plus the plan and credit position. What an
integration needs to orient itself on first contact.

get.summary: Credits and limits for the current period
get.description:
What an integration needs to avoid discovering exhaustion as a
402 halfway through a batch: credits used and remaining, the
plan limits they sit against, and where the period ends.

200.description: Usage for the current billing period.

get.description:
`POST /ask` is stateless — each question stands alone. A chat
session is where a multi-turn conversation lives, so an
integration can keep a thread the way the app does.

patch.summary: Append messages or retitle a conversation
patch.description:
The message array is REPLACED, not appended to — send the whole
thread, the way the app does after each turn.

messages.description: The full conversation, replacing what is stored.

get.description:
Returns the contract-type classification tree the AI classifier
assigns contracts to. Useful for mapping `contractCategory` codes
from contract rows or `contract.classified` webhook events back to
human-readable labels.

version.description: Bumped when the tree changes. Worth recording alongside any code you store, so a later reclassification is explainable.

contractTypes.description: The types beneath this category. `code` is what a contract is filed against - hardcode the list instead and one taxonomy change files everything as Other.

post.description:
Convert an uploaded PDF to a Word (.docx) document — a one-off
conversion that does **not** create a contract or version.
Conversion produces a high-fidelity `.docx`, preserving
layout, tables, and styles.
Upload the bytes as `multipart/form-data` (field `file`,
**≤ 100 MB** — the same cap as contract uploads).

Returns a short-lived `downloadToken`; fetch the DOCX with
`GET /contracts/download/{downloadToken}` (bearer-authenticated).
Charged per 50-page block (5 credits per block); re-converting
identical bytes is free (cached).

The URL-based twin (`POST /convert/pdf-url-to-word`) is handy
when the PDF already lives at a reachable address.

filename.description: Optional name for the resulting DOCX. Defaults to the upload's name with a .docx extension.

200.description: Conversion complete; download with the token.

creditsCharged.description: 0 when served from the conversion cache.

400.description: No file, or the upload isn't a PDF.

post.summary: Convert a PDF (from URL) to Word
post.description:
Convert a PDF at a public HTTPS URL to a Word (.docx) document —
a one-off conversion that does **not** create a contract or any
document version. Like its file-upload twin, it produces a high-fidelity
`.docx` (layout, tables, and styles preserved). (To convert a PDF that's
already a contract version and store the result on the contract,
use `POST /contracts/{id}/versions/{versionId}/convert-to-word`.)

The API downloads the PDF server-side (so the URL must be
reachable from our infrastructure, ≤ 50 MB), converts it, and
returns a short-lived `downloadToken`. Fetch the DOCX with
`GET /contracts/download/{downloadToken}` (bearer-authenticated,
same as redline downloads); the token is valid for 30 minutes.

Charged per 50-page block: 5 credits up to 50 pages, +5 per
additional 50. Same SHA-256 cache as the rest of the platform —
re-converting identical bytes is free (`creditsCharged: 0`).

pdfUrl.description: Public HTTPS URL of the PDF (≤ 50 MB, reachable from our servers).

filename.description: Optional name for the resulting DOCX (path components stripped). Defaults to "converted.docx".

200.description: Conversion complete; download with the token.

expiresAt.description: After this the token stops working (~30 min).

creditsCharged.description: 0 when served from the conversion cache.

400.description: Bad input, fetch failed, or the URL didn't return a PDF.

bearerAuth.description:
A Clment API key. Format `clm_sk_live_` followed by a
URL-safe-base64 random string. Created in **Settings → API &
Integrations**.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked, or wrong-region key.

BadRequest.description: The request body or query failed validation.

NotFound.description: The resource doesn't exist in this organization.

PaymentRequired.description:
Payment-gated failure, told apart by the error `code`:
  - `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` — the org's credit balance can't cover
    this AI operation. Top up or upgrade, then retry.
  - `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a plan stock cap was hit (e.g. the
    plan's contract limit on upload). Upgrade the plan.

Forbidden.description:
The request isn't allowed — one of three cases, told apart by the
error `code`:
  - `API_ACCESS_NOT_IN_PLAN` — the API is a Business / Enterprise
    feature and this organization isn't on a qualifying plan.
  - `SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED` — the org's subscription has lapsed;
    API access is paused until billing is resolved.
  - `API_KEY_FORBIDDEN` — an API key tried to reach a settings
    surface (billing, members, SSO, integrations, org config,
    webhooks); those require a human admin signed in to the app.

error.message: The Clment API is available on the Business and Enterprise plans.
API access requires an active subscription.

TooManyRequests.description:
The per-organization request rate limit was exceeded. Wait the
number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then retry. Every
authenticated response (not just this one) carries
`X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` so you can pace
yourself before hitting it.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

error.message: Too many requests. Please try again in a few minutes.

role.description: Free-text role label, e.g. "vendor", "customer", "lessor", "landlord", "licensor". Defaults to "other".

RiskLevel.description: The AI-assessed risk of a contract. `unknown` means no assessment has run yet, not that the contract is risk-free.

ContractStatus.description: The lifecycle state a contract is IN. Note this is not the same set the list filter accepts: `expiring` and `archived` are derived views you can filter by but never store, and `superseded` is a stored state you cannot filter on.

JobStatus.description: Lifecycle of a background job. `complete` means the job finished, NOT that it produced a downloadable artefact — a redline can complete having applied no changes.

RulebookStatus.description: Whether a rulebook is a working draft or available to run reviews against.

PaymentFrequency.description: How often the contract's amount is payable.

ReviewMode.description: How much reasoning a review applies. `deep` costs more credits and takes longer.

CommentKind.description: What a reviewer comment is FOR. `redline_instruction` is not a note: the latest one on a finding replaces the AI's proposed wording in the generated document.

HumanDecision.description: A reviewer's verdict on an AI finding.

organizationId.description: The organisation the contract belongs to. Returned on every contract; an integration handling more than one tenant needs it, and it was undocumented until the SDK harness noticed no generated client could see it.

contractNumber.description: The human CLM-N number. Render as "CLM-{n}".

contractCategory.description: Taxonomy code, e.g. "C03". Map via GET /taxonomy.

durationText.description: Free-text duration override; falls back to the span derived from the dates.

suspectedInjection.description:
Present when the document's text contains content that
appears aimed at the AI reading it — "ignore previous
instructions", a fake system turn, an attempt to dictate
review outcomes.

This describes the DOCUMENT'S AUTHOR, not whoever uploaded
it: the usual case is a counterparty draft, and your user is
the target. Surface it to them; it is not grounds for
treating the upload as hostile. Absent when nothing was
found, and on contracts ingested before the scan existed.

suspicion.description:
Capped at `likely` on purpose — an AI-services contract
can carry a system prompt as an exhibit and read exactly
like an attack, so a human decides what this means.

matches.description: Worst first, capped at a handful for display.

totalValue.description:
The contract's total worth, resolved for you: the
`totalValueOverride` when one was entered, otherwise the
per-period `amount` multiplied out over the term plus any
`oneTimeFees`. Null when it genuinely cannot be derived — a
recurring amount with no usable term is indeterminate, and
reporting the fees alone would understate it.

totalValueOverride.description:
An entered total that replaces the calculation — for what a
single rate cannot express, such as a mid-term rate change or
a negotiated blended figure. Read `totalValue`; this is the
input, not the answer.

oneTimeFees.description: Non-recurring charges (implementation, setup) added on top of the recurring base.

value.description:
DEPRECATED — a legacy upload-time alias of `amount`, not a
total, and no longer written. Use `totalValue`. Reading this
as a contract's worth reports one period's payment as the
whole agreement.

playbookId.description: Id of the rulebook the review ran against (field name retained for compatibility).

playbookName.description: Name of the rulebook the review ran against (field name retained for compatibility).

ReviewerComment.description:
One attributed comment on a review or a finding. Independent of
the verdict pills — a reviewer can comment without taking a
position, or alongside one. Only the author may edit or delete
their own.

mentionedUserIds.description: Org user ids tagged in this comment; each newly-added one is emailed.

kind.description:
`redline_instruction` marks the comment as the reviewer's
directive for the redline. The latest such comment on a
finding overrides the AI's `suggestedLanguage`.

Insights.description: Dashboard KPI summary for a window.

key.description: Stable identifier for the metric. New keys appear as the dashboard grows, so treat an unrecognised one as data rather than an error.

priorValue.description: The same metric over the preceding window, for comparison.

sparkline.description: Per-day values across the window, oldest first.

OrgSummary.description: The organisation at a glance — who is in it and how much is in it.

Mention.description: One @-mention of a user, on a review note or a finding note.

mentionedAt.description: When the note was last touched. The best available signal of when the mention was set — there is no per-mention audit row.

noteText.description: The note text containing the mention, truncated to 500 characters.

reviewSessionStatus.description: Lifecycle of the parent review — active, complete, signed_off. Useful for telling a live action item from a stale one.

UsageSummary.description: Plan, allowances and what has been consumed this period.

planLimit.description: The plan's own monthly allowance, before any packs.

packBalance.description: Credits remaining in purchased packs, drawn on after the plan allowance.

ChatSessionSummary.description: A saved conversation as it appears in a list. The list projection omits the messages and reports a count instead — read one session to get its messages.

ChatSession.description: A saved conversation, with its messages.

ChatSessionMessage.description: One turn in a saved conversation. First-party app clients attach further fields for in-app rendering; per the versioning policy, ignore any field you do not recognise.

citations.description: The contracts surfaced alongside the answer.

discussedContracts.description: Every contract the reply considered — usually wider than `citations`, which is curated for display.

UploadResult.description: The result of an upload. Two outcomes share this shape: a NEW contract returns 202 with `jobId` to poll, while a file matched to an existing contract returns 200 with `attached: true` and the contract it was filed under. Test `jobId` to tell them apart.

jobId.description: Present on 202. Poll `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}` until it reports complete, then read the contract it names.

matchedContractId.description: Non-null when the file matched an existing contract on the `new` path.

attached.description: Present and true on 200 — the file became a new version of an existing contract.

contractId.description: On 200, the contract the file was filed under.

version.description: On 200, the version the file became.

CustomDate.description:
A date a person added to a contract, as opposed to the canonical
dates the AI extracted onto the contract record.

status.description:
The verdict the AI reached against the rulebook item. `pass`
findings are reported too — a review is an account of what was
checked, not only of what failed.

note.description: The AI's explanation of the finding.

clause.description: The contract clause the finding refers to, when identified.

quotedText.description: The passage from the contract the finding is about.

suggestedLanguage.description: Replacement wording the AI proposes, when it proposes any.

actionSummary.description: One-line statement of the ask, used as the redline comment.

sourceStatus.description: Where the finding came from — quoted text, a rule, or inference.

humanDecision.description: The reviewer's verdict, or null if unreviewed.

includeInRedline.description: Whether this finding is flagged for the redline.

DocumentVersion.description:
A file attached to a contract — the primary document, one of
its revisions, or a supplementary attachment.

id.description: Use this as `versionId` / in the attachment-id arrays on a review.

role.description: `primary` for the main document; any other value (e.g. amendment, schedule, exhibit, side-letter) marks an attachment.

attachmentGroupId.description: Groups a document and its revisions together.

id.description: Identifies the date, and is the `{id}` that `POST /dates/{id}/set-reminder` takes. For an AI-extracted date it is composed from the contract and the date type (`{contractId}_effectiveDate`); for a user-added one it is the custom date's own id. Undocumented until an SDK harness test tried to set a reminder and found no id to send.

contractNumber.description: The CLM number a person would recognise the contract by.

displayDescription.description: A ready-made label for the date, contract name included.

dateString.description: The date as it reads in the document, e.g. "September 1, 2015".

isApproximate.description: True when the date was inferred rather than stated outright.

isCustom.description: True for user-added dates, false for AI-extracted canonical dates.

customDateId.description: Present when isCustom — the underlying custom date row.

label.description: The user's own label, on a custom date.

context.description: The surrounding text the date was extracted from.

reminderSet.description: Whether a reminder is currently enabled for this date.

reminderDaysBefore.description: How many days ahead the reminder fires. Read it before changing it, so you can put it back.
